ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the perimeter of $\triangle ACD$ is $14$, $AB-AC=2$, and the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ intersects $AB$ at point $D$ and intersects $BC$ at point $E$. Find the lengths of $AB$ and $AC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since the perimeter of $\triangle ACD$ is 14,\\
$\therefore AC+AD+CD=14$,\\
because $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $BC$,\\
$\therefore BD=CD$,\\
$\therefore AC+AD+BD=14$,\\
$\therefore AC+AB=14$,\\
since $AB-AC=2$,\\
$\therefore AB=\boxed{8}$, $AC=\boxed{6}$.
